The Default Game lasts four Eras, each consisting of setup for the Era, three simultaneous-selection action cycles, shared Power and Production, a Public Audit, and scoring one revealed Era Mandate. Kestralyn’s infrastructure identity is concrete: its first completed Facility Build each Era costs 1 less Runway and scores 1 Mandate when that discount actually reduces the payment; its once-per-game Orbital Compute ability can relocate a Facility globally during movement, possibly producing it immediately, but adds 2 Scrutiny. rulesReconstruction: SETUP — Build the 13-tile board with Frontier in the center. Randomize the six specified operational tiles into the inner ring and the six specified public tiles into the outer positions. Tiles remain fixed for all four Eras. Every non-Frontier tile has two Facility spaces; Frontier has none.

Prepare four Era areas. For each Era, shuffle only Headlines without an Advanced Play badge and place that deck beside its Era card. Three Headlines will be revealed per Era, producing a 12-card Future Timeline. Divide the 12 Era Mandates into four three-card decks, shuffle each separately, and place it with its Era. Shuffle the 50-card Training deck.

Put the shared resources, contract pairs, Systemic Risk cubes, Audit bag, Power references, Initiative marker, and Fusion marker within reach. The Audit bag starts empty; all player-colored Scrutiny cubes begin outside it. Do not use Tactics, secret objectives, Reserve Specialists, or any Advanced Play procedure.

For Kestralyn, take Jiwon Park, three Teams, four Facilities, one Generator, the six Core Actions, seven Escalations, declaration card, ten Scrutiny cubes, track markers, and resources. Set the board to 6 Runway, 3 Compute, 0 Capability, 0 Customers, 2 Trust, and 0 Safety. Put 2 already-earned Mandate on the public track; this is awarded only once.

Place every CEO and one Team at Frontier; keep Kestralyn’s other two Teams in supply. Facilities and the Generator appear to remain in supply until constructed, although the treatment of the first Facility’s starting-grid identifier needs confirmation. Add every faction’s printed starting Trust and record that total as Setup Collective Trust. Randomly assign Initiative, then begin Era I.

ERA OPENING — Advance to the fixed Era card, read its New this Era strip, reveal exactly one of its three Mandate cards, and return the other two unseen. Ready all six Core Actions. Award Escalation availability: 0 in Era I, 1 in Era II, 1 in Era III, and 2 in Era IV. Previously unlocked, unused Escalations remain available, but unspent availability expires at Era end.

UNLOCKS — Era I teaches normal movement, Core Actions, Training, the starting grid, Facilities, Customers, and Scrutiny. Era II unlocks ordinary Generators, Mega-Clusters, Reorganization, and Escalation use. Era III unlocks Joint Ventures, immediate Power purchases, Open Weights, and Narrative Capture. Era IV unlocks Agent Swarm, Declare AGI, Fusion Demonstrator, and faction signature programs such as Kestralyn’s Orbital Compute.

EACH OF THREE CYCLES — Reveal and resolve one Headline before selection, placing it face up in the current Future Timeline row. Its named effect applies at its printed timing and normally expires after the cycle unless it explicitly names Production, the Era, or the rest of the game.

Everyone secretly selects one unused Core Action, or spends one Escalation availability to select an unlocked, unused Escalation. Reveal simultaneously and resolve clockwise from Initiative. On resolution, choose one CEO or Team, move it 0–2 adjacent hexes, then resolve only the selected card from the destination. Selection commits the card, but the piece, route, mode, target, payment, and immediate trade are chosen during resolution.

A committed action cannot be replaced if another player consumes its target first. Movement still happens and the card exhausts without compensation. After resolving, exhaust a Core Action; for an Escalation, reduce availability and flip that once-per-game card. Pass Initiative clockwise after the cycle.

Immediately before or after Act, the active player may make one complete trade offer to one rival involving Runway, Compute, and/or Safety. The rival accepts, rejects, or makes one complete counteroffer; the original player then accepts or rejects. There is no redirection or further countering. Accepted resources move immediately, promises are non-binding, and caps apply immediately.

MOVEMENT AND MAP — CEOs provide 2 presence; Teams and Facilities provide 1. Most presence controls a hex, while a tie means no controller. The acting piece’s destination governs construction, Research, Deploy, Influence, and one applicable visit bonus. Pieces may coexist and there is no combat. Frontier offers an optional after-Act gain of 1 Runway plus 1 Scrutiny.

CORE ACTIONS — Fund either gains 2 Runway or gains 4 Runway and adds 2 Scrutiny; Allocation Exchange adds 1 Runway. Research spends 1 Compute and reveals Training cards one at a time, gaining provisional Capability for unique domains. After a non-duplicate, stop and bank or continue. An unprotected duplicate crashes the run, loses provisional Capability, and adds 1 Scrutiny. Safety or Research Commons can protect a normally protectable duplicate, but immediately ends the run by banking. Special Training cards modify this procedure as printed.

Build either constructs a Facility for 2 Runway on the acting piece’s non-Frontier hex or, from Era II onward, constructs Kestralyn’s single ordinary Generator on an Energy hex. Power Corridor builds a 4-Power Emergency Power Complex for 1 Runway, which adds 1 Scrutiny every Production. Thermal and Water Basin builds a 3-Power Civic Heat Battery for 2 Runway and immediately gains 1 Trust. Shared Energy hexes have three Generator slots.

For Kestralyn, the first completed Facility Build each Era costs 1 less Runway. If that discount actually reduces the amount paid, immediately score 1 Mandate. This normally makes the first Facility cost 1; at Fabrication Corridor, its separate 1-Runway Build discount may reduce the final cost further under the universal cost order, but the interaction should be confirmed from the physical card wording.

Organize recruits a Team at the acting piece’s destination for 2 Runway and then moves one CEO or Team up to two more steps; or distributes five movement steps among CEOs and Teams; or pays 1 Runway to move a Facility at the destination to an adjacent legal space. A relocated Facility carries attached identifiers and contract tokens but immediately loses Grid-Ready status and has Power eligibility recalculated.

Deploy spends 1 Compute and gains the next Customer if Kestralyn meets its Capability threshold: 2, 4, 6, 8, then 10. Human Access District waives the Compute cost. Each Deploy normally adds 1 Scrutiny. Customers produce 1 Runway each during Production and immediately score Mandate: 2 each for Customers 1–3 and 1 each for Customers 4–5.

Influence moves normally, then either gains Trust or removes Scrutiny at Consensus Network, Civic Permission Authority, or Allocation Exchange, with the printed enhanced result at the first two; or, from Era III, creates or terminates a Joint Venture from one of the acting player’s Facilities. A proposed cross-player agreement requires explicit consent and cannot be redirected after rejection.

POWER — Kestralyn’s starting grid supplies exactly 1 dedicated Power to its designated first Facility. It cannot be sold or supply Mega-Cluster demand. An ordinary Generator powers only eligible Facilities on its own or adjacent hexes; Facilities do not relay Power. A Facility requires 1 Power to produce. Power is reassigned each Production and never stored.

END-OF-ERA POWER AND PRODUCTION — Resolve each Production box for every player before moving to the next box, ordinarily in Initiative order. Generate: determine local Generator eligibility; every connected Generator operates automatically, and every Emergency Power Complex adds 1 Scrutiny. Apply any Headline generation effect here too. Generators create capacity, not stored resource tokens automatically gained by their owner unless Facilities convert it through production or it is sold in the Trade box effect described next as capacity transfer/payment exchange rather than stored Power itself. Trade: from Era III, each player may make one Power-purchase request to one adjacent rival connection. If accepted, the buyer pays 1 Runway per Power; each supplier may sell at most 1 installed Generator/Fusion Power this Production. Starting-grid and emergency Power cannot be sold. Allocate: combine legal starting-grid, Generator, purchased, and emergency capacity, assigning each unit once to eligible Facilities and Mega-Clusters. Flip fully powered Facilities to Grid-Ready and all insufficiently powered Facilities to normal. Produce: powered Facilities resolve their tile production, then each Customer produces 1 Runway, then active Mega-Clusters produce. Partner: active Joint Ventures produce in ascending token-number order. Apply resource caps after every gain: 12 Runway, 10 Compute, and 3 Safety for Kestralyn unless its board says otherwise. Facility production is determined by its district, such as 2 Compute at Compute Estate, 2 Runway at Allocation Exchange, or 1 Compute plus 1 Runway at Fabrication Corridor. Workforce Transition instead allows a Team move during Production; Consensus Network and Thermal and Water Basin remove Scrutiny before Audit; Civic Permission Authority gains Trust; Research Commons gains Safety; Power Corridor gains Compute; Human Access gains Runway. Resolve the exact printed district entry when its powered Facility produces. Joint Ventures require two fixed rival Facilities in range and powered during Production; each partner gains the contract-icon resource shown on the other host’s tile. Contracts remain owned but become inactive whenever their fixed hosts fail the position or Power requirements. Mega-Clusters require two adjacent hosts and 2 additional Power beyond powering both Facilities. A solo project costs 3 Runway and 2 Compute and produces 3 Compute when all demand is met. A joint project splits construction and Power demand between consenting lead and partner; full production gives the lead 2 Compute and partner 1. Construction adds 2 Scrutiny. Kestralyn’s once-per-game Orbital Compute becomes available in Era IV. During its movement step, it replaces acting-piece movement by moving one Facility to any legal open Facility space, carrying attachments. Recalculate Power eligibility; if sufficient currently available capacity can power it, resolve its printed production once immediately. Add 2 Scrutiny. The precise meaning of currently available capacity outside Production deserves clarification before relying on it. PUBLIC AUDIT — Draw the number of cubes based on player count and Era. At the stated 3–5 suggested counts, the draws are: three players 2/2/3/4, four players 2/3/4/5, and five players 3/4/5/6 across Eras I–IV. Stop early if the bag empties. In Eras I–III, each Kestralyn cube drawn makes Kestralyn pay 1 Runway or lose 1 Trust, using the available option if only one exists. In Era IV, each cube requires an indivisible payment of 2 Runway or loss of 1 Mandate. If fewer than 2 Runway are available, lose Mandate if possible; at 0 Mandate, reduce Runway to 0. Drawn colored cubes return to their owners; undrawn cubes remain in the bag. A black Systemic Risk cube penalizes every player with at least 3 Customers using the current Era penalty, then returns to supply. Black cubes left in the bag after Era IV matter to the World Ending. If Kestralyn must add Scrutiny while all ten cubes are already in the bag, pay 1 Runway or lose 1 Trust for each unavailable cube. Depletion never cancels the risky effect. SCORE THE ERA MANDATE — Check only the revealed Mandate’s printed qualification and criterion. If nobody qualifies, nobody scores. Otherwise, one qualifying leader scores 2 Mandate; tied qualifying leaders each score 1. Do not use public score, resources, or control as an unprinted tiebreaker. Leave the card visible as history. Then expire unspent Escalation availability and any effects whose printed duration ends with the Era, and begin the next Era. MANDATE SCORING THROUGHOUT PLAY — Score immediately on the public track: Customers award 2/2/2/1/1; first reaching Capability 3, 6, 9, and 12 awards 2 each; first reaching Trust 2, 4, and 6 awards 2 each; and cards, Mandates, declarations, Fusion, and faction abilities score as printed. Kestralyn starts at Trust 2 and already begins with its printed public Mandate, so the Trust-2 threshold should not be awarded again during setup unless the faction board explicitly indicates otherwise. Threshold awards are permanent even if the track later falls. No Facilities, territory, stored resources, or unused cards convert to score unless a printed effect says so. ERA IV ESCALATIONS — Agent Swarm requires two different unused Core Actions, moves once, resolves both from one destination in either order, permits only one visit bonus, exhausts both, and adds 3 Scrutiny. Declare AGI requires Capability 9, 3 Customers, 3 already Grid-Ready Facilities, Trust 2, and 3 Compute. It is global after normal movement; check requirements on resolution. The first valid declaration scores 7 Mandate, later ones 5, and each adds 3 Scrutiny. A Facility built during Era IV cannot become Grid-Ready until that Era’s Production, which occurs after actions, so it cannot support an Era IV declaration. Fusion requires the acting piece to end on Power Corridor, 5 Runway, and a free Generator slot there. It provides 6 Power, scores 2 Mandate, adds 3 Scrutiny, and does not consume Kestralyn’s ordinary Generator-piece allowance. GAME END — After Era IV’s Production, Audit, and Mandate scoring, read all 12 Headlines aloud in Era order. Then every player loses 1 Mandate per offline Facility, never falling below 0. There is no other endgame score conversion. Determine the shared World Ending separately. AGI emerges only if at least one institution that declared finishes at Capability 9 or more. The ending is Open only if final combined Trust is at least Setup Collective Trust plus player count and unresolved black Systemic Risk in the Audit bag is lower than player count. Otherwise it is Closed. AGI plus Open gives The Singularity; AGI plus Closed gives The Closed Loop; no AGI plus Open gives The Plural Future; no AGI plus Closed gives Assured Continuity. Read that ending narrative, then announce the institution with the most Mandate. Ties break by higher Trust, then more Customers, then more Compute, then joint victory with the prescribed merger announcement.
anticipatedFriction: Kestralyn wants to build repeatedly, but each new Facility needs local Power to produce and avoid the final offline penalty. The dedicated starting grid powers only the designated first Facility; later Facilities need a suitably placed Generator, purchased Power after Era III, or emergency capacity from a Headline.

The infrastructure-compounder sequence is timing-sensitive: Generator construction does not unlock until Era II, Production occurs only after all three cycles, and a Facility does not become Grid-Ready merely because Power appears available. It must receive complete demand during a completed Production.

Kestralyn’s discounted first Facility can score 1 Mandate in every Era, but only if the Facility is successfully completed and the discount actually reduces payment. Limited Facility spaces and Initiative order can turn a committed Build into an exhausted no-effect action.

Mega-Clusters consume much more Power than their visible pair of Facilities suggests: both hosts need their ordinary Facility demand plus 2 additional Power. Starting-grid Power cannot cover the additional demand.

A joint Mega-Cluster or Joint Venture depends on explicit rival consent and fixed named hosts. A refusal consumes the attempted Escalation in the Mega-Cluster case, and neither proposal may simply be redirected to a new partner.

Orbital Compute can rescue or reposition an infrastructure network, but relocation strips Grid-Ready, can deactivate contracts or a Mega-Cluster, and adds 2 Scrutiny. Its immediate-production clause is unusually dependent on how available Power is tracked between Production phases.

Only three action selections are available per Era, despite having six Core Actions. Building, powering, researching, deploying, and political cleanup compete for those slots. Escalations replace an ordinary selection unless Agent Swarm specifically consumes two unused Core Actions.

Research is a push-your-luck source of Capability. A duplicate can erase the entire run’s provisional Capability, while Kestralyn has no native duplicate protection. Safety production or visiting Research Commons matters if the infrastructure plan also needs reliable Deploy thresholds.

Scrutiny persists in the bag until drawn or removed. Infrastructure pushes—venture funding, Mega-Clusters, emergency power, Fusion, Orbital Compute, and AGI—can compound Audit exposure, with the Era IV penalty attacking Mandate rather than Trust.
Mandate leaders and lowest/highest-player effects can change with Initiative. Because Initiative passes every cycle, Seat 2 has no permanent order advantage.

The exact revealed Mandate can pull the plan in different directions. An infrastructure-heavy board is naturally relevant to powered-Facility, Power-demand, Compute-production, and control Mandates, but scoring uses only the currently revealed card and often requires tracking gains or successful runs throughout the Era.
Resource caps are immediate. Large Production chains can waste Runway or Compute if Kestralyn reaches 12 or 10 before later Facility, Mega-Cluster, or Joint Venture production resolves.

Offline Facilities still occupy spaces and give presence, but produce nothing and each cost 1 Mandate at game end. An ambitious fourth Facility can therefore become a liability if the local network cannot support it in the final Production.

Each Core Action is normally usable once per Era: Fund gains 2 Runway, or 4 Runway plus 2 Scrutiny; Research spends 1 Compute for a push-your-luck Training Run; Build constructs a Facility, or from Era II a Generator; Organize recruits, redistributes people, or relocates a Facility; Deploy spends 1 Compute and gains the next Customer if Capability is sufficient; Influence gains Trust/removes Scrutiny at political districts or creates/terminates a Joint Venture from one of your Facilities.

Research: reveal Training cards individually. Each first ordinary domain adds 1 provisional Capability; Curated Corpus becomes a missing ordinary domain; the first Synthetic Loop is the unique Loop domain; Benchmark Leak adds 2 provisional Capability and 1 Scrutiny; Licensed Dataset requires 1 Runway to continue or forces banking; Human Evaluation gives 1 Trust and immediately banks. After a non-duplicate, stop and bank or continue. An unprotected duplicate loses all provisional Capability and adds 1 Scrutiny. Safety or a Research Commons visit may protect a protectable duplicate, but immediately ends the run by banking; the next duplicate after Synthetic Loop is unprotectable.

Facilities cost 2 Runway, occupy one of two spaces on any non-Frontier destination, and require 1 delivered Power to produce. Fabrication Corridor discounts Build by 1. Generators unlock in Capacity, require the acting piece on an Energy hex, occupy one of three shared Generator slots, and each player may own one ordinary Generator. Power Corridor builds a 4-Power Emergency Power Complex for 1 Runway; Thermal and Water Basin builds a 3-Power Civic Heat Battery for 2 Runway and grants 1 Trust.

Deploy thresholds for Customers 1–5 are Capability 2/4/6/8/10. Customers immediately score Mandate 2/2/2/1/1, add one Scrutiny per Deploy, and each produces 1 Runway during Production. Human Access District waives the Compute cost.

Presence controls a hex only when one player has strictly the most presence; tied hexes are uncontrolled. Control matters only when a card or effect names it and does not itself score endgame Mandate.

Immediate trade window: immediately before or after Act, the active player may make one complete Runway/Compute/Safety offer to one rival. The rival accepts, rejects, or makes one complete counteroffer; the original player then accepts or rejects. No redirecting or repeated bargaining. Accepted resources move immediately and caps apply.
Corthaven’s passive ability: whenever another player spends at least 2 Compute in a single action, gain 1 Runway, at most twice per Era. Track this per action, not per token or payment component.

Corthaven’s Allocation Window: once during Era II only, after a Headline resolves and before selection, create 2 temporary Compute. Offer each token separately to a named rival for a Runway price no higher than their current Runway. They accept, reject, or counter once with a lower price; you then accept or reject. There is no replacement buyer. All temporary Compute disappears at cycle end wherever it is, so buyers must spend it that cycle or lose it.

Escalations: spend 1 availability when selecting an unlocked card, resolve it instead of a Core Action, then flip it. Each named Escalation is usable once per player per game. Capacity unlocks Mega-Cluster and Reorganization; Authority unlocks Open Weights and Narrative Capture; Continuity unlocks Agent Swarm, Declare AGI, and Fusion Demonstrator.

Mega-Cluster uses two adjacent host Facilities and costs 3 Runway plus 2 Compute solo, adding 2 Scrutiny. It demands normal Power for both hosts plus 2 extra Power and produces 3 Compute. A joint version splits cost and output: Corthaven as lead pays 2 Runway/1 Compute and gains 2 Compute; partner pays 1 Runway/1 Compute and gains 1 Compute. Each powers its host plus 1 extra demand. Rejection consumes the Escalation. Hosts must remain adjacent and locally Power-eligible appropriate to their owners. Reorganization moves every Team up to one hex and may return one Team for 3 Runway plus 1 Scrutiny; it is not another Action resolution test for The Shovels unless an actual action payment of at least 2 Compute occurs elsewhere under a card effect that qualifies as one action spend claim (clarification recommended). General rules establish The Shovels by another player's spend in one action; Reorganization itself spends none. Open Weights gives everyone 1 Capability while you gain 2 Trust and remove 1 Scrutiny. Narrative Capture removes 2 of your Scrutiny, gains 2 Runway, or gives 1 Scrutiny to a player with more Customers than you. Agent Swarm requires two different unused Core Actions, moves once, resolves both at the same destination in either order, applies the visit bonus to only one, exhausts both, and adds 3 Scrutiny. Declare AGI requires Capability 9+, 3+ Customers, 3+ Grid-Ready Facilities, Trust 2+, and 3 Compute; first valid declaration scores 7 Mandate, later ones 5, and each adds 3 Scrutiny. Fusion requires ending movement at Power Corridor and paying 5 Runway; it occupies a Generator slot, supplies 6 Power, scores 2 Mandate, adds 3 Scrutiny, and is additional to the one ordinary Generator limit. Mega-Cluster and Reorganization wording should be resolved from their individual cards; The Shovels triggers only when a rival actually spends the threshold in an action, most clearly Mega-Cluster's solo 2-Compute payment or other modified actions reaching 2 Compute. Reorganization itself does not spend Compute. Open Weights, Narrative Capture, Agent Swarm, Declare AGI, and Fusion follow their printed resolutions as detailed above. Agent Swarm resolves two actions but is itself the selected Escalation; ask whether a rival spending 2+ Compute across the two component actions is evaluated separately or collectively for Corthaven's passive (the phrase “in one action” suggests separately). Declare AGI is once per player because its Escalation flips; the game continues after it. Fusion's Power is local to its own/adjacent Facilities under normal eligibility. Reorganization's optional returned Team comes from any Team after movement because the rule does not state a location restriction. Open Weights' Capability can cross a threshold and immediately score normal Capability Mandate. Narrative Capture can target only a player currently having more Customers. A rejected joint Mega-Cluster attempt consumes availability and flips the card. The printed AGI card can be reversed as a visible declaration record after success. Fusion is blocked if all Power Corridor Generator slots are occupied. Mega-Cluster construction requires the acting piece to end on either host hex. Joint Venture creation requires consent and an available numbered pair; either party may later spend Influence solely to terminate it. Default Joint Ventures require adjacent rival Facilities and both hosts powered during Production; each partner receives the contract icon shown on the other host’s district. Each accepted project grants consent only to that project. Contracts travel with moved Facilities but become inactive if their spatial or Power requirements fail. Contract output is not full district production. Power cannot be stored or relayed through Facilities. Your starting grid supplies only the identified first Facility. Each Generator supplies Facilities on its own or adjacent hex; its capacity is allocated only once. Offline Facilities remain present and may recover in later Production. During Authority and later, a player may request purchased Power only from an adjacent rival connection, following the Production trade window. End-of-Era Resolution begins after the third action cycle with five synchronized Power and Production boxes. Generate: identify each Generator’s local recipients; connected Generators operate automatically, Emergency Power adds 1 Scrutiny, and Headline generation applies. Trade: in Initiative order, each player may request Power from one adjacent rival connection; an accepted buyer pays 1 Runway per Power, while each supplier can sell at most 1 installed Generator/Fusion Power. Starting-grid and emergency Power cannot be sold. Allocate: total legal starting-grid, Generator, purchased, and emergency Power and assign it to legal Facilities/projects. Flip every fully powered Facility Grid-Ready and every insufficient one normal. Produce: powered Facilities resolve their district output, then each Customer yields 1 Runway, then active Mega-Clusters produce. Partner: active Joint Ventures produce in ascending token-number order. Apply resource caps after every gain: Runway 12, Compute 10, Safety 3. After Production, conduct the Public Audit. Draw by player count and Era; for the suggested 3–5 players the Era I–IV profiles are 3 players: 2/2/3/4, 4 players: 2/3/4/5, and 5 players: 3/4/5/6. Stop if the bag empties. Drawn colored cubes return to their owners; undrawn cubes stay in the bag. In Eras I–III, each cube makes its owner pay 1 Runway or lose 1 Trust. In Era IV, pay an indivisible 2 Runway or lose 1 Mandate; with fewer than 2 Runway, lose Mandate if possible, otherwise reduce Runway to zero. A black Systemic Risk cube penalizes every player with at least 3 Customers using that Era’s penalty, then returns to supply. Consensus Network Facilities remove Scrutiny before the draw. If a risky effect requires a cube after all ten of yours are already in the bag, immediately pay 1 Runway or lose 1 Trust instead. Score the revealed Era Mandate after Audit. If nobody meets its printed qualification, no one scores. A sole qualifying leader earns 2 Mandate; tied qualifying leaders earn 1 each. Compare only the printed criterion and leave the card beside its Era. Then begin the next Era; after Continuity’s Mandate, proceed to final scoring. Mandate also scores immediately during play: Customer awards; 2 at the first reach of Capability 3/6/9/12; 2 at the first reach of Trust 2/4/6; and printed Headline, faction, Mandate, Fusion, or AGI awards. Threshold awards never reverse. Facilities, resources, control, unused cards, and contracts have no unprinted conversion. Game end: read all twelve Headlines aloud in Era order. Each player loses 1 Mandate per offline Facility, never below zero. Then determine the World Ending from visible state. AGI emerges only if at least one declaring institution ends with Capability 9+. The world is Open only if final combined Trust is at least Setup Collective Trust plus player count and unresolved black cubes remaining in the bag are fewer than the player count. Otherwise it is Closed. AGI+Open is The Singularity; AGI+Closed is The Closed Loop; no AGI+Open is The Plural Future; no AGI+Closed is Assured Continuity. Read that narrative, then announce the highest-Mandate winner. Break ties by Trust, Customers, Compute, then joint victory with the stated merger announcement.
anticipatedFriction: The first Facility is mechanically important but starts in supply. Mark it clearly and construct it before another Corthaven Facility unless the physical identifier makes the ordering unambiguous; otherwise players may accidentally assign the dedicated starting grid retroactively.

The first-Facility wording is slightly awkward: setup grants a grid, but no Facility exists until Build. The most natural reading is that the component bearing the integrated identifier is the fixed recipient whenever constructed, not whichever Facility happens to be built first.
Only three of six Core Actions are normally used each Era. Players may mistakenly play all six, refresh cards each cycle, or believe unused actions carry an extra benefit.

Initiative passes after every complete cycle, not after each individual resolution. It controls resolution order and unresolved targeted ties, which makes simultaneous competition for the last Facility space, Generator slot, or contract pair consequential.
A revealed Action can fizzle after rivals act. Players should confirm scarce targets and payments during resolution but cannot switch cards after the reveal.

Grid-Ready is earned only during completed Production. Building or reconnecting a Facility does not immediately make it Grid-Ready, so an Era IV Facility cannot support an AGI declaration that same Era.

Power accounting is easy to overstate: Facility demand, Mega-Cluster extra demand, starting-grid restrictions, Generator locality, purchased capacity, and Grid-Ready state should be tracked separately.
Production proceeds box-by-box across all players. Letting one player complete all five boxes early can invalidate Power sales, allocations, contracts, and Audit removals.

Corthaven’s Allocation Window happens after one Capacity Headline but before that cycle’s selection, only once in the Era. Temporary Compute expires at cycle end even after sale, creating a strict use-it-now negotiation.

Corthaven gains from another player spending 2+ Compute in one action, not from total spending across a cycle or Production. Joint Mega-Cluster payments of only 1 Compute do not reach the threshold; a 2-Compute solo Mega-Cluster clearly does.
Removing Scrutiny means retrieving your cubes from the bag, not merely reducing a board track. This can be overlooked because the cubes are hidden once added.
The Audit choice is constrained by affordability. In Era IV, a player with only 1 Runway cannot voluntarily pay it toward the 2-Runway penalty; they lose Mandate if possible.

Default-only Authority content appears internally inconsistent: the Era card says Civic Permission Authority votes are added by Advanced Play, yet several unbadged Headline cards call a “Civic Permission Authority vote,” and no Default vote procedure is supplied. Those cards cannot be executed from the frozen Default rules without clarification.

Some Mandates describe only a leader criterion and do not state an explicit numerical minimum, despite the general rule referring to minimum qualification. Zero-activity ties could therefore be disputed.

The End-of-Era sequence is labeled in prose rather than as a single heading: Power and Production, Public Audit, then Score the Mandate. Do all three after every Era, including Era IV, before final scoring.

Final winner and World Ending are separate. An AGI declarer need not win; the Mandate winner does not determine the shared ending; and a declaration ceases to count for emergence if no declaring player finishes at Capability 9+.

The rules say to count AGI declarations for the World Ending but the emergence test only needs at least one qualifying declarer. The raw count appears narratively relevant but does not otherwise alter the matrix.

The game requests narrative text from World and Institutions after deriving the ending. If that companion is not on the table, the mechanical result remains determinable but the instructed ending reading is unavailable.

questions.text: Which physical Facility is Corthaven’s fixed “first Facility,” and must I build that marked piece before any of my other three Facilities?
questions.reason: The starting grid is dedicated to the integrated identifier, but the rules do not explicitly state whether construction order is mandatory or whether the marked Facility can remain unbuilt while another is built first.

questions.text: What exact Default Game procedure resolves an unbadged Headline that says “Civic Permission Authority vote”?
questions.reason: The Authority Era card assigns those votes to Advanced Play, while the frozen Default Headline pool appears to include vote cards and the Default rules provide no ballot, electorate, tie, or outcome-selection procedure.

questions.text: For Era Mandates with no printed minimum—such as most Capability gained—does a zero-to-zero tie qualify and give everyone 1 Mandate, or does nobody qualify?
questions.reason: The general rule requires a printed minimum, but several cards provide only a comparison criterion.

questions.text: When Agent Swarm causes a rival to spend Compute across two component Core Actions, does The Shovels test each component Action separately or their combined spending?
questions.reason: Agent Swarm is the selected Escalation but resolves two Core Actions; “spends at least 2 Compute in one action” is ambiguous at that boundary.

questions.text: Does a Corthaven temporary Compute token sold during Allocation Window count normally as the buyer’s Compute when they spend it, including triggering The Shovels if at least two are spent in one action?
questions.reason: The tokens transfer and disappear only at cycle end, but their interaction with ordinary spending triggers is not stated explicitly.

questions.text: May Corthaven offer both temporary Compute tokens to the same rival, resolving two separate offers, or must the named rival differ for each token?
questions.reason: The ability says to make one offer per token and names “a rival,” but does not impose or reject a repeat-buyer restriction.

questions.text: If the Allocation Window buyer cannot legally spend a purchased temporary Compute token after reveal because an earlier player takes the last target, does it simply disappear at cycle end?
questions.reason: The normal blocked-action rule gives no compensation, but confirming that it also governs these paid temporary resources would prevent a negotiation dispute.

questions.text: For Power purchases, what precisely constitutes an “adjacent rival Power connection”: adjacent Generators, adjacent eligible Facilities, or a buyer Facility adjacent to a rival Generator/Fusion?
questions.reason: Default Game rejects a Network graph, yet the Production rule uses “connection” without defining the exact two components whose adjacency permits a request.
